title: Check engine light flashing
h1: Why is my check engine light flashing?
metaDesc: Check engine light flashing or blinking? It usually means a serious misfire. Answer a few questions to see what's likely causing it and what to do right now.
synonyms: blinking check engine light and car shaking
check engine light flashing while driving
check engine light flashing then stops
check engine light flashing car jerking
can i drive with a flashing check engine light
check engine light flashing and car shaking
intro: A flashing check engine light is the engine computer's most urgent warning. It usually means the engine is misfiring badly enough to damage the catalytic converter, and in the worst cases overheat the exhaust. Answer a few questions to see what's likely going on and what to do right now.
safety: If the light is flashing, or the engine is shaking, pull over as soon as it's safe and turn the engine off.
If you smell raw fuel or burning, or see smoke from under the car or hood, pull over as soon as it's safe, turn the engine off and get everyone away from the car.
If the temperature gauge reaches red, pull over and turn the engine off. Don't open the radiator cap while it's hot.

q_now.q: Is the light flashing right now with the engine running?
q_now.help: Flashing means blinking on and off about once a second. A light that stays lit without blinking is a steady check engine light, which is usually less urgent.

opts.a: Yes, and the engine is shaking, stumbling or losing power
Yes, but the engine feels fairly normal
It flashed earlier, but now it's steady or off

q_shaking.q: Does the engine feel like it's shaking, stumbling or jerking, especially when you press the gas?

opts.a: I smell raw fuel or burning, or see smoke
The temperature gauge is high, or I've been losing coolant
It started right after filling up with fuel, or after running very low
Only when accelerating hard, climbing a hill or carrying a heavy load
Only right after a cold start, then it settled down
Just once, and it hasn't happened since

result.title: The engine may be misfiring badly. Stop driving it now
result.now: Pull over where it's safe, turn off the engine, and have the car towed or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If you're on a highway, get to the shoulder or the next safe exit with gentle throttle and your hazard lights on, then turn the engine off.
If you smell fuel or burning, or see smoke, step away from the car and call for help.
If the temperature gauge climbs toward red or a red warning light comes on, pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: A flashing light with shaking usually means one or more cylinders aren't firing. Unburned fuel goes into the exhaust and burns in the catalytic converter, which can overheat it within minutes. Every mile you drive raises the repair bill and the fire risk. A shop will check misfire data by cylinder and test the coil, plug and injector before replacing anything.

causes.name: Failed ignition coil
causes.clues: A sudden, steady miss that's worse when accelerating.

causes.name: Worn or fouled spark plug
causes.clues: High miles since the last spark plug change, or the miss has been building over time.

causes.name: Fuel injector stuck or not firing
causes.clues: A fuel smell, or the miss is just as bad at idle.

causes.name: Mechanical engine problem
causes.clues: Ticking or knocking, or a timing belt or chain that's due.

you: Note when the shaking is worst: at idle, when accelerating, or all the time.
Don't restart the engine just to test it.
shop: Code scan and misfire counts by cylinder
Ignition coil and spark plug test

result.title: A misfire may be happening even if you can't feel it. Don't keep driving
result.now: Pull over where it's safe and turn off the engine. Have the car towed or call roadside assistance (your insurer, a motor club, or the number in your owner's manual).
if: If you're in heavy traffic, ease off the gas, avoid hard acceleration, and get off the road at the first safe spot.
If the light goes steady after a restart, the fault is still stored. Have the code read before driving any distance.
If you smell raw fuel or burning, or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and get everyone away from the car.
result.why: The computer flashes the light when it counts enough misfires to risk overheating the catalytic converter. A misfire on one cylinder isn't always easy to feel, especially at steady speed, but the damage to the converter still happens.

causes.name: Failing ignition coil or spark plug
causes.clues: A slight stumble under load or at idle.

causes.name: Fuel injector problem
causes.clues: A faint fuel smell, or worse fuel mileage lately.

causes.name: Vacuum leak
causes.clues: A hissing sound from the engine bay.

you: Note whether there's a hesitation when you accelerate.
Listen for hissing from the engine bay with the engine off and cool.
shop: Code scan and misfire counts by cylinder
Ignition coil and spark plug test

result.title: Fuel or exhaust heat may be creating a fire risk
result.now: Pull over, turn off the engine, get everyone out and away from the car, and call for help.
if: If you see smoke or flames, stay well back and call 911.
If the smell fades and there's no smoke, still don't restart it. Have it towed.
result.why: A severe misfire sends raw fuel into a very hot exhaust. That can make the catalytic converter glow red-hot and ignite anything nearby, like dry grass under the car. A fuel smell can also mean a leak near hot engine parts.

causes.name: Overheated catalytic converter from misfire
causes.clues: A burning or sulfur smell from under the car.

causes.name: Leaking fuel injector or fuel line
causes.clues: A strong raw fuel smell under the hood.

causes.name: Oil or fluid on hot exhaust
causes.clues: Bluish smoke, or a burning oil smell.

result.title: Coolant may be getting into the engine
result.now: Pull over, turn off the engine, and have the car towed. Don't open the radiator cap while the engine is hot.
if: If you see white, sweet-smelling smoke from the exhaust, mention it to the shop. It can point to coolant burning in the engine.
If the coolant level is low once it's fully cool, don't top it up and restart to test it.
result.why: A misfire together with overheating or coolant loss can mean coolant is leaking into a cylinder, for example through a failed head gasket. Coolant doesn't burn, so that cylinder misfires. Driving on it can warp the engine and cause major damage. A shop will pressure-test the cooling system and test for combustion gases before deciding what has failed.

causes.name: Failed head gasket
causes.clues: White exhaust smoke, a sweet smell, or bubbles in the coolant reservoir.

causes.name: Cracked cylinder head or intake gasket leak
causes.clues: Coolant loss with no visible leak.

causes.name: Overheating causing misfires
causes.clues: The temperature gauge climbed before the light started flashing.

you: Once the engine is fully cool, check the coolant level in the reservoir.
Note any white smoke or sweet smell.

result.title: Bad or wrong fuel, or fuel starvation, may be causing the misfire
result.now: Pull over where it's safe, turn off the engine, and have the car towed. Tell the shop where and when you filled up.
if: If you think the wrong fuel went in (like diesel in a gas car), don't restart it. The tank may need draining.
If it happened when the tank was nearly empty, add fuel, but still have it checked before driving.
If you smell raw fuel or burning, or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and get everyone away from the car.
result.why: Water in the fuel, the wrong fuel, or a fuel pump struggling on an almost-empty tank can all leave the engine without the right mixture. That causes misfires across several cylinders at once, which flashes the light.

causes.name: Contaminated or wrong fuel
causes.clues: It began within a few miles of filling up.

causes.name: Fuel starvation from a very low tank or weak pump
causes.clues: The gauge was near empty, or it's worse going uphill or around corners.

causes.name: Clogged fuel filter or injectors
causes.clues: Gradual loss of power over time before this.

you: Keep your fuel receipt and note the station and pump.
Note how much fuel was in the tank before it started.

result.title: A worn spark part may be failing (ignition coil or spark plugs)
result.now: If the light flashes again or the engine shakes hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Otherwise: Get it checked within a few days. Until then, drive gently, avoid hard acceleration and steep hills, and don't tow or haul anything.
if: If the light flashes again or the car shakes, pull over and turn the engine off.
If it's happening more often, stop driving it and have it checked right away.
If you smell raw fuel or burning, or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and get everyone away from the car.
If the temperature gauge climbs toward red or a red warning light comes on, pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: Spark plugs and coils need more energy to fire when the engine is working hard. A weak coil or worn plug can cope at light throttle but misfire under load. A shop will usually swap or test the coil and inspect the plugs to confirm which one is at fault, and the repair is often fairly simple if it's done before the catalytic converter is damaged.

causes.name: Weak ignition coil
causes.clues: A stumble or jerk when accelerating or going uphill.

causes.name: Worn spark plugs
causes.clues: High miles since they were last changed.

causes.name: Fuel delivery weakness
causes.clues: A general loss of power at higher speeds too.

you: Check your service records for the last spark plug change.
shop: Code scan and misfire counts by cylinder
Ignition coil test or swap test

result.title: A cold-start misfire may be a coil, plug or injector starting to fail
result.now: If the light flashes again or the engine shakes hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Otherwise: Get it checked within a few days. Don't drive off while the engine is shaking. If it shakes on a cold start, wait until it runs smoothly, and if it doesn't settle within a minute or two, turn it off and get it checked.
if: If the light flashes while you're driving, pull over and turn the engine off.
If you notice coolant loss or white exhaust smoke at startup, have it checked right away.
If you smell raw fuel or burning, or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and get everyone away from the car.
result.why: A cold engine is harder to fire, so a weak coil, worn plug or leaky injector often shows up there first. A misfire that only happens cold and then clears up is an early warning that often gets worse. The stored code and a few tests will show which part is involved.

causes.name: Weak ignition coil or worn spark plug
causes.clues: Worse in cold or damp weather.

causes.name: Leaking or sticking fuel injector
causes.clues: A fuel smell at startup.

causes.name: Small coolant leak into a cylinder
causes.clues: White smoke at startup, or coolant slowly going down.

you: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold.
Note the outside temperature when it happens.
shop: Cooling system pressure test if coolant is dropping

result.title: The misfire may come back. Get the code read soon
result.now: If the light flashes again or the engine shakes hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Otherwise: Have the stored code read within a few days. Drive gently and keep trips short until then.
if: If the light flashes again, pull over and turn the engine off.
If the light is now steady, follow the same plan: get the code read soon.
If you smell raw fuel or burning, or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and get everyone away from the car.
If the temperature gauge climbs toward red or a red warning light comes on, pull over and turn the engine off.
result.why: The computer stores a misfire code even after the light stops flashing. A one-time flash often comes from a part that's starting to fail, and it's usually much cheaper to fix now than after it damages the catalytic converter.

causes.name: Ignition coil or spark plug starting to fail
causes.clues: A brief stumble when it flashed.

causes.name: One-off fuel or moisture problem
causes.clues: It happened in heavy rain or right after a fill-up.

causes.name: Loose connector on a coil or injector
causes.clues: Recent engine work.

you: Note the conditions when it flashed.
shop: Code scan including stored misfire data
Ignition coil and spark plug inspection

result.title: Check the light now: if it's blinking, stop driving
result.now: If the light is blinking, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. If it's steady and the car drives normally, have the code read within a few days.
if: If the light blinks at any point, treat it as urgent: pull over, turn the engine off and have it towed.
If it's steady and the car drives normally, it's usually less urgent, but still get the code read.
If you smell raw fuel or burning, or see smoke, pull over, turn the engine off and get everyone away from the car.
result.why: A flashing light and a steady light mean very different things. Flashing means a misfire that can damage the catalytic converter right now. Steady means a fault worth checking, which is usually not an emergency unless the car runs poorly or other warning lights come on.

causes.name: Misfire
causes.clues: The light blinks, often with shaking.
causes.against: A smooth-running engine with a steady light makes a severe misfire less likely.

causes.name: Emissions or sensor fault
causes.clues: The light is steady and the car drives normally.

you: Watch whether the light is blinking or steady.
